solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Babywear is refunded when returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the phrase for being paid back is read backwards

parts.note: money that is refunded is repaid

explanation.surface: A shop note promising that baby clothes brought back get your money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like part of the refund story, but it tells you to read REPAID backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nappy, as Americans call it, is an item a baby wears, so it counts as babywear.

clue.text: One gets slim, half-heartedly running

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the heart of the word for slim is its doubled middle letter, and half of that heart is dropped

parts.note: slim means narrow

explanation.surface: Someone loses weight by jogging without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two R's at the centre of NARROW, leaving NAROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Events running one after another happen consecutively, which is the idiom 'three wins on the trot'.

clue.text: This writer's abandoning fresh material

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the writer's letters are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky or insolent
the setter refers to themself as this writer; this writer is = I'm

explanation.surface: An author gives up on new subject matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a noun for fabric or content, but it is the adjective meaning relevant, as in 'material evidence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something material to a case is relevant to it, a synonym for being to the point.

clue.text: Sunken ship uncovered by seaweed is this shape

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a sunken ship is a wreck
tangle is a type of kelp, a large brown seaweed

explanation.surface: A sunken wreck stripped of its weed turns out to have a particular outline.
explanation.walkthrough: TANGLE, a kind of kelp, is a less familiar word for seaweed; 'by' places REC beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a four-sided figure with right angles, the shape the wordplay points to as 'this'.

clue.text: It could be submarine port

definitions.meaning: a submarine is a long filled roll, often called a sub, a kind of filled bread snack
a town in Kent, one of the old Cinque Ports on the English coast

explanation.surface: A vessel that might be a sub is in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich in Kent is one of the historic Cinque Ports of south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine roll is an example of a filled-bread snack, and the Kent town was a historic harbour.

clue.text: Mark traps American bear

indicators.note: traps means holds inside, so the word for mark encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a mark is a stain

explanation.surface: A stain catches an American bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load or loss is to endure or support it, a synonym for keeping up under strain.

clue.text: Not acceptable, whichever way you look at it

definitions.note: the two-word phrase for unacceptable is a palindrome, its letters reading identically either way

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the clue says the letters read the same forwards and backwards, however you view them

parts.note: the two-word phrase for unacceptable is a palindrome, its letters reading identically either way

explanation.surface: Something is unacceptable from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'whichever way you look at it' is literal: the answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase means something is not acceptable or not allowed.

clue.text: Dispute created by weapon beginning to end

indicators.note: the letter at the beginning is moved to the end of the word for the weapon

parts.note: a sword is a weapon

explanation.surface: A quarrel started by a weapon running from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' sends the S of SWORD to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words with someone is the idiom for an argument or dispute.

clue.text: Tin basin wrongly presented as pot

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: wrongly means arranged incorrectly, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A tin bowl is mistakenly passed off as a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges BASIN to NABIS. 'pot' is a kitchen pot in the surface but slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is the slang name for the drug made from the hemp plant.

clue.text: Save stretchers for military quarters

parts.note: save in the sense of except, like bar
racks were instruments that stretched victims

explanation.surface: Keep the medical stretchers for the army's living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb but is the preposition meaning except, as in 'all save one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings where soldiers live, their military accommodation.

clue.text: Italian city associated with German mathematician

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian city is linked with a German mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' seems to describe the mathematician, but it only gives G; Alan Turing was English.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing was the British mathematician and codebreaker who founded computer science.

clue.text: Laugh out loud at one backward-looking novel

parts.note: LOL is the texting abbreviation for laugh out loud

indicators.note: backward-looking means facing the other way, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone laughs out loud at a novel that dwells on the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-looking' seems to describe the novel, but it reverses AT and I to give ITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is Vladimir Nabokov's 1955 novel.

clue.text: I'm a case struggling to retain recollection, ultimately

definitions.text: I'm a case struggling to retain recollection, ultimately

indicators.note: to retain means to hold inside, so one letter goes within the shuffled letters
struggling suggests the letters are in disarray and get rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A patient admits to being a hard case who can barely remember anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: someone who struggles to retain memory is exactly the person described.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with memory loss struggles to retain recollection, which the whole clue describes as a patient's own words.

clue.text: Heroine periodically reveals age

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A heroine now and then lets slip how old she is.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of HEROINE give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period of time, a synonym for an age.

clue.text: One entertained by e.g. genuine comic opera

indicators.note: entertained by means received as a guest, so this word sits inside the rearranged letters
comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is amused by a truly funny opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' signals the anagram and 'entertained by' the insertion; the opera is in fact tragic, so 'comic' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's 1879 opera is based on Pushkin's verse novel.

clue.text: Lavishly dressed up on telly

indicators.note: dressed means prepared or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone appears on television in lavish costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' looks like part of the picture of costume, but it rearranges UP ON TELLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something lavishly is to do it with rich abundance, which is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Winning goal standing, initially disallowed

parts.note: a goal is an aim or end

indicators.note: the first letter is not allowed, so it is removed from the word for standing

parts.note: standing in the sense of bearing or posture

explanation.surface: A match-winning goal is allowed to stand after first being ruled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' and 'goal' suggest football; 'Winning' means charming, and 'goal' is END.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is charming and lovable, a synonym for appealing.

clue.text: Aunt Sally perhaps is a legitimate target

definitions.meaning: Aunt Sally is a traditional pub or fete game of throwing sticks at a figure, so an example of a game at a fair
someone who can rightly be attacked or criticised

explanation.surface: Aunt Sally is a fair target for criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game where players throw at a dummy's head; figuratively, it is someone set up for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for someone or something it is reasonable to attack, and literally an amusement at a fete.

clue.text: What could make tablet an area of contention?

parts.note: read the instruction as a word for war, then ground (crushed, so rearranged), whose letters reshuffle into the clue's last word

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what would turn a pill into a source of dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as instructions, gives a word for war that is ground (rearranged) into TABLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of fighting, literally or figuratively, is an area where sides are in dispute.

clue.text: Hit bar son, and drink!

indicators.note: bar means except, so the letter for son is left out

parts.note: to hit is to slap

explanation.surface: Someone strikes the bar's son and orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it means without.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals drink by lapping, so to lap water is to drink it with the tongue.

clue.text: Repair or put back in warehouse?

definitions.meaning: repair means renovate or bring back to a former state
read as ..., to store again in a warehouse

explanation.surface: Should something be fixed or returned to the stockroom?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as RE-STORE, to put into store again.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair a building or artwork is to renovate it, and a warehouse holds goods in storage.

clue.text: Look lasciviously around church? He might

definitions.text: Look lasciviously around church? He might

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for church goes inside

parts.note: to leer is to look lasciviously

explanation.surface: A man eyes people up lustfully around a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a man given to lust might well leer around church.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who is excessively lustful is one who would leer, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Intrusion requires lock to protect resort

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the resort sits inside the lock

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A break-in calls for a lock to guard a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Going onto land without permission is trespass, an unlawful intrusion.

clue.text: Extinguish, needing small then large amount of water

parts.note: a lake is a large body of water

explanation.surface: Putting out a fire takes a small then a large amount of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extinguish' suggests a fire, but the answer quenches thirst.
explanation.definitionFit: To quench a thirst or put out a desire is to satisfy it completely.

clue.text: Region in which action ultimately takes place?

definitions.text: Region in which action ultimately takes place?

indicators.note: in which says the last letter goes inside the word for region

parts.note: a region is an area

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A query about the place where the action finally happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a sporting or political stage is where the action happens.
explanation.definitionFit: An area for contests or sport is the scene where the action takes place.

clue.text: Protector of crown prince nameless? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, so the letters are found within it

explanation.surface: The guardian of a royal crown, a prince with no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' suggests royalty, but it is the crown of a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer coating of a tooth protects its crown, the part above the gum.

clue.text: Get on? Staff get on

parts.note: to staff a desk is to man it
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: A question about getting along is answered by employees growing older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' appears twice: first meaning cope, then meaning grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on with something is to cope or get by, a synonym for coping.

clue.text: Unmitigated thug involved with riot

indicators.note: involved means mixed up together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A total thug takes part in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the letters of THUG and RIOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmitigated is total or complete, as in an unmitigated disaster.

clue.text: Agent needs key — she's close by entrance

parts.note: DEL is the delete key on a keyboard

indicators.note: close means the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: read as she with 's for is, a link
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A spy needs a key and a woman close by the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she's close' is she is close: only she gives a letter, its last one.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a representative who acts on behalf of others, as an agent does.

clue.text: Go back into tent for food

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the reversed word goes within the tent

parts.note: a yurt is a round tent used by nomads in Central Asia

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the letters of go run the other way

explanation.surface: Head back into the tent to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A yurt is the felt-covered round tent of Central Asian nomads.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a fermented milk product eaten as food.
